value.rationale: The natural induced Lipschitz norm is solved exactly for the full family of connected complete multipartite graphs. The theorem proves a surprising largest-part universality and totally orders all graphs of fixed order by their sharp heat amplification. It gives a two-vertex sharp nonexpansivity boundary, unique transient peak and norming inputs, plus a nontrivial continuum limit depending on the asymptotic largest-part proportion, with global sharp supremum 2. Such exact finite-time behavior and phase geometry cannot be recovered from ordinary Markov positivity or curvature inequalities alone.
